description: CosmicVision is a solo space-tech initiative focused on exploring innovative solutions using NASA's open data. I am a Computer Science student interested in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Vision and data analysis. For NASA Space Apps 2026, I aim to develop FireWatch, a satellite-based wildfire intelligence system using MODIS and VIIRS hotspot data to analyse and visualise fire activity.
summary: **FireWatch – Satellite-Based Wildfire Intelligence System** is a Python-based project developed by Team Asteroid for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, under Challenge 09: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots. The project aims to bring active-fire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellites into a common platform for easier visualization and analysis. Using Python, Pandas, Streamlit and Folium, FireWatch processes NASA FIRMS datasets, harmonizes common data fields, and displays hotspot locations through an interactive map. It also provides date and sensor filters, daily fire activity charts, Fire Radiative Power (FRP) statistics, CSV export and spatial nearest-neighbour comparison between MODIS and VIIRS observations. The analysed South Asia dataset contained 4,635 records, including 249 MODIS and 4,386 VIIRS observations for November 15, 2026. At a 1 km spatial threshold, 62 MODIS records and 132 VIIRS records had a nearest observation from the other sensor within that distance. These results provide an exploratory comparison of satellite detections rather than confirmation of individual fire events. FireWatch aims to make multi-sensor satellite hotspot information easier to explore and understand.
details:
FireWatch is a satellite-based wildfire intelligence system developed to make active-fire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS instruments easier to explore and compare. The project addresses the challenge of working with hotspot information from different satellite sources by bringing their common attributes into a consistent data structure while preserving their individual sensor identities.

The application is developed using Python, Pandas, Streamlit and Folium. It processes NASA FIRMS CSV datasets, validates geographic coordinates and acquisition dates, and organizes important information such as latitude, longitude, satellite, sensor, confidence, acquisition time and Fire Radiative Power (FRP). The processed observations are displayed on an interactive map, allowing users to explore hotspot locations, filter records by sensor and date, view daily fire activity, compare satellite detection counts and download the harmonized dataset.

FireWatch also includes a MODIS–VIIRS spatial comparison module that uses the Haversine distance formula to identify observations located near each other on the same acquisition date. In our South Asia dataset for November 15, 2026, the application processed 4,635 valid observations, including 249 MODIS and 4,386 VIIRS records. Using a 1 km proximity threshold, 62 MODIS observations and 132 VIIRS observations had a nearest observation from the other sensor within that distance.

The project aims to make satellite hotspot information more accessible and useful for exploring regional fire activity. It is an exploratory analysis tool; nearby detections are not necessarily the same fire event, and a satellite hotspot does not automatically confirm a wildfire on the ground. Future improvements include multi-day historical analysis, time-aware satellite comparisons and more detailed regional analysis.
